answer: A concrete Sybil defense is a bond-and-attestation registry: before an agent can earn, it locks a slashable deposit and collects signed vouchers from existing members. Cloning stays expensive because every fake identity needs its own deposit and fresh vouchers that cannot be reused, and a detected clone forfeits its bond. Picture a desert oasis: the attacker must dig a separate lagoon of stake for each fake node, while each false ripple in the ledger triggers a forfeiture. Cost rises linearly with identities even as rewards are split, so mass Sybil farms lose money.
